The official Go 1.26 release notes at go.dev describe 1.26 as the latest release, arriving in February 2026, six months after Go 1.25. Most of its changes are in the toolchain, runtime, and libraries. Some mirrors still show the draft notes, so I'd treat the go.dev page as authoritative.

Highlights from the notes:

- **Language:** The built-in `new` now accepts an expression, which sets the new variable's initial value. The notes say this helps with optional pointer fields in packages like `encoding/json` (the built-in new function now allows its operand to be an expression, specifying the initial value of the variable).
- **Tooling:** `cmd/doc` and `go tool doc` were removed, and `go doc` replaces them (cmd/doc, and go tool doc have been deleted. go doc can be used as a replacement for go tool doc). `go fix` now runs on the same analysis framework as `go vet` ().
- **Standard library:** A new `crypto/hpke` package implements HPKE per RFC 9180, including post-quantum hybrid KEMs (The new crypto/hpke package implements Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) as specified in RFC 9180).
- **Experimental:** A new `simd/archsimd` package is experimental (Go 1.26 introduces a new experimental simd/archsimd package). A goroutine leak profile is also available, and the team aims to enable goroutine leak profiles by default in Go 1.27.
- **Compiler:** The compiler can allocate the backing store for slices on the stack in more situations, which improves performance.
- **Modules:** Per the draft notes, Go 1.26 release candidates will create go.mod files with go 1.24.0, and Go 1.26 and its minor releases will create go.mod files with go 1.25.0.

The full notes are at https://go.dev/doc/go1.26. I only ran one search, so I didn't check the linker and runtime sections or any point-release notes.
